q7.answer: The refresh thread replaces the in-memory snapshot whole. Clients keep no copy of the key. On every outbound request each client calls secrets.get('<name>') and puts the current value in the Authorization header. A refreshed key therefore applies to the next request with no restart, and no request sees a mix of old and new snapshots.

q8.answer: Using evidence, not elapsed time. Every running pod must show the new version id for all three keys in the secret_version_in_use metric. Every pod's last refresh success must be newer than the last store write. No pod may report a refresh warning. No old-image pod may exist, including workers and cron jobs. The provider dashboard must show no unaccounted traffic on the old key after a quiet period. Step 12 first proves refresh works by writing a new version of one secret.

q9.answer: First, set up store access, KMS keys and namespaces, and verify them (step 7). Second, rotate at the providers by creating new keys with the old ones still active, and copy the new keys into the store (step 8). Third, ship one PR that switches the app to read from the store, removes api_key from config/app.yaml and adds the CI guard (step 9). Staging soak (step 10), prod rolling deploy (step 11) and a prod refresh proof (step 12) follow. Old images are then blocked (step 13), and last the old keys are revoked at the providers (step 14). Removing the keys from the file happens in the same PR as the code switch, not as a separate later step.

q10.answer: make run sets APP_ENV=dev. The app loads config/app.yaml plus config/app.dev.yaml, which points at provider sandboxes. It reads orders-api/dev/* from the store using the engineer's own identity. These are sandbox keys, and engineers cannot read the prod path. APP_ENV=dev-offline is an alternative that uses local mock providers with fixed dummy keys.

q11.answer: A startup attempt counts as successful only if all three secrets are fetched and non-empty. If one is missing, the attempt fails. The instance waits 2 seconds and retries, up to 3 retries (4 attempts in total). It then logs the error class and exits non-zero (e.g. code 70). /healthz keeps returning 503 until then, so the pod never becomes ready. A partial snapshot is never used.
